task: Implement solution.py, a Python CLI that audits simultaneous reservations within a reporting window. It reads a single JSON object from stdin and emits a summary of occupancy. Use only Python's standard library.

approved_plan.goal: Report the duration, peak and alert ranges for reservations within one time window.
acceptance_criteria: Require an object with window, threshold and intervals. A window or reservation is a JSON array of exactly two integer endpoints [start,end] with start < end. Endpoints may be negative. Booleans and floats do not qualify as integers. threshold must be a positive integer and intervals an array. Ignore extra object keys.

Interpret all ranges as start-inclusive and end-exclusive. Intersect each reservation with the window. Reservations outside the window contribute zero. Validate every supplied reservation, including those outside the window.
Count each input row separately, including duplicates. Input ordering has no significance.
covered is the total duration inside the window during which at least one reservation is active.
peak is the maximum number of simultaneous reservations inside the window. first_peak is the earliest time at which this maximum occurs; when peak is zero use null.

alerts is the chronological list of maximal half-open ranges where occupancy is at least threshold. Merge adjacent qualifying spans even when their occupancy counts differ. Use an empty array when none qualify.

On success exit zero and print one JSON object with exactly covered, peak, first_peak and alerts. JSON formatting and key order are immaterial. Malformed JSON or any invalid input must exit nonzero and produce no stdout. Stderr is unspecified.
implementation_steps: Parse and validate the entire input.
Compute occupancy across the window and derive all four output fields.
Serialize the result or signal invalid input through the documented CLI.
test_strategy: Exercise the observable success and failure contracts through stdin and stdout.

interface_contract: Run python3 solution.py from the project root. The 7 numbered acceptance criteria define the entire public contract. No importable API is promised.
